caption:
A chief economist at Apollo says AI has shown no financial payoff outside the tech sector. Revenue per worker and profit margins are rising for the Mag 7 but flat for the S&P 493. Mainstream companies are starting to treat token spending as a cost center.

TechCrunch's AI graveyard list adds another data point: about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.

What I see in companies is rarely a model problem. The pilot works in a demo, but it never lands in the daily workflow. Nobody owns the result, and nobody measures it.

I lived this with AskMoses.AI, the AI sales-coaching SaaS I built end to end and run as a contractor. 17 organizations in the US signed up and 6 actually use it. 11 of 17 never activated, because onboarding required a CRM and a rubric before delivering any value.

Launching is not the same as being used. AI only pays off when it lands in a real workflow and someone tracks the result.
